taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: AD CS certificate template enrollment and identity authority
controls.source_trace: Determine which low-privilege principal can enroll or modify a template and what identity/purpose a resulting certificate would represent.
controls.implementation_branch: Evaluate template enrollment rights, subject/SAN control, issuance requirements, EKUs and CA policy together. A permissive-looking template alone does not establish a usable authentication certificate. Use exported configuration or an isolated lab to trace the exact claimed principal and relying service; do not enroll certificates impersonating real directory users.
controls.operational_method: Retain CA/DC build and patch level, template issuance/enrollment settings, certificate SID/strong mapping evidence and the actual relying authentication protocol. A SAN selected by a caller is not enough to decide accepted identity under current strong-mapping enforcement. Compare a deliberately mapped synthetic identity with a mapping-mismatched certificate in supplied traces or an isolated directory lab; certificate issuance, successful mapping and final service authorization are separate necessary edges. Do not request impersonation certificates for real principals.
controls.controlled_verification: Use an owned lab CA or configuration proof with synthetic identities; compare intended enrollment and an out-of-policy subject/purpose request.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A risky-looking template flag alone does not establish effective enrollment or certificate-based authentication to a protected service.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Constrain enrollment/template authority and issuance identity, verifying intended certificate workflows and denied impersonation.
